latin.context: Aaj Mangalvar hai. Priya ne kal kaha tha, 'Kal mera interview hai.' Priya ki saheli Ritu use aaj pooch rahi hai, 'Toh tera interview kaisa gaya?'

devanagari.context: आज मंगलवार है। प्रिया ने कल कहा था, 'कल मेरा इंटरव्यू है।' प्रिया की सहेली रितु उसे आज पूछ रही है, 'तो तेरा इंटरव्यू कैसा गया?'

english.context: Today is Tuesday. Yesterday Priya had said, 'My interview is tomorrow.' Priya's friend Ritu is asking her today, 'So how did your interview go?'
english.question: When was Priya's interview?

items.explanation: Priya spoke on Monday (yesterday relative to today's Tuesday) and said 'kal' (tomorrow) meaning Tuesday but Ritu's question 'kaisa gaya' (how did it go) confirms it is already over, placing the interview on Monday. The deictic anchor shifts: 'kal' in Priya's speech meant the next day from Monday, i.e. Tuesday, but from today's (Tuesday's) perspective it happened today. Wait re-anchoring: Priya spoke yesterday (Monday) and said 'kal mera interview hai', meaning her interview was on Tuesday. But Ritu asks today (Tuesday) 'how did it go', implying it happened today or is done. The correct answer is Tuesday (today), making option A correct.

cultural_markers: deictic tense shift in reported speech
